title: Environment retrospective
description: Retrospective on a coding session that proposes changes to the agent's ENVIRONMENT, not to the product: a deterministic pass reads the Claude Code transcript, the planning record and git history into friction signals (retro-signals) and an inventory of the checks already in place (retro-inventory); only when the weighted signal sum reaches retro.signal_threshold is a fresh gsd-retro-analyst worth running. Candidates are laid out by kind — mechanical → a check (project lint rule, hook, gate, verify_gates), judgement → reviewer skills (agent_skills.*), never CLAUDE.md, environment → settings — each tied to a signal and checked against the inventory. Nothing is applied automatically: the report is written to .planning/retro/ and a human routes each candidate. Accepted checks are journaled in .planning/retro/CHECKS.json so a check that never fires becomes a removal candidate. Claude Code only; every other runtime is degraded to git and .planning evidence and says so (ADR-5209).

retro.enabled.description: Enable the retro capability: the `gsd-tools retro` commands and /gsd-retro. Every read is local and read-only, and nothing a retro produces is applied without a human (ADR-5209), so it is on by default; set false to keep transcripts out of GSD entirely.

retro.auto.description: What `gsd-tools retro signals --decide` answers once the signal sum reaches retro.signal_threshold: suggest (print one line proposing /gsd-retro), auto (the caller may spawn gsd-retro-analyst itself — its candidates are still never applied), or off (always skip). Below the threshold the answer is skip in every mode.

retro.signal_threshold.description: Weighted friction score at or above which a retro is worth a model pass (score >= threshold). Each signal scores weight × (count − min + 1); see src/retro-signals.cts for the weights.

retro.repeat_call_min.description: Identical tool calls in one session before they count as a repeated-call signal (at least this many).

retro.repeat_error_min.description: Occurrences of the same tool error before it counts as a repeated-tool-error signal.

retro.reread_min.description: Reads of one file with no edit to it in between before they count as a reread signal.

retro.edit_churn_min.description: Edits of one file in one session before they count as an edit-churn signal.

retro.nav_streak_min.description: Navigation calls (Read/Grep/Glob and read-only shell) in a row with no edit before they count as a nav-streak signal.

retro.checker_loop_min.description: Plan-checker spawns in one session before they count as a plan-checker revision loop.

retro.checkpoint_min.description: Checkpoints reached in one session before they count as a repeated-checkpoint signal.

retro.hook_block_min.description: Blocks by the same hook before they count as a hook-block signal.

retro.excerpt_window.description: Transcript events on either side of a signal that the analyst is shown instead of the transcript.

retro.max_signals.description: Signals listed in a report; the rest are enumerated by id in `omitted`, never dropped silently. Caps the list, never the score.

retro.excerpt_chars.description: Maximum length of a redacted excerpt that leaves the transcript reader.

retro.check_stale_days.description: A check journaled in .planning/retro/CHECKS.json that has not fired in the transcripts of this many days (and was accepted at least this long ago) is offered as a removal candidate. Removal, like acceptance, is a human decision.
